days.title: Wealth tax
days.desc: An annual tax on total net assets above a high threshold.
days.note: Heavy redistribution puts it hard left. It asks little of personal freedom, so it sits close to the middle on the vertical.

days.title: Tariffs
days.desc: Taxes on imported goods to protect home industry.
days.note: Once a free-trade-right target, now backed by the nationalist right and parts of the left. The state steering trade pulls it up the grid.

days.title: Conscription
days.desc: The state requires adults to serve in the military for a period.
days.note: The state orders people into service, which makes it strongly authoritarian. The slight right lean reflects who usually proposes it.

days.title: Legalising all drugs
days.desc: Ending criminal penalties for possession and sale.
days.note: Left and right libertarians both back it, so it lands near the economic middle and far down the grid.

days.title: Universal basic income
days.desc: A regular cash payment to every adult with no conditions.
days.note: Left on economics because it redistributes. It leans libertarian because it removes means tests and case workers.

days.title: Rent control
days.desc: A legal cap on how much landlords can raise rents.
days.note: Market intervention on behalf of tenants is left economics. Dictating prices to private owners adds an authoritarian tilt.

days.title: Nuclear power
days.desc: State-backed expansion of nuclear energy.
days.note: Not a clean left-right issue. Large state projects lean authoritarian, while pro-industry support leans right.

days.title: Compulsory voting
days.desc: Citizens are fined for not turning up to vote.
days.note: Compelling behaviour is authoritarian. It has little economic content so it stays near the centre line.

days.title: Bernard Sanders
days.desc: U.S. Senator, VT (Independent). Scored on the 119th Congress.
days.note: Placed from roll-call voting. DW-NOMINATE dimension 1 (-0.55) is economic left-right. Dimension 2 (-0.43) captures other cross-cutting issues and is only a rough stand-in for libertarian-authoritarian.
days.source: Voteview DW-NOMINATE (Lewis, Poole, Rosenthal et al.)

days.title: Conservative Party
days.desc: Vote share at the most recent election: 23.7%.
days.note: Experts rated this party 7.4/10 on economics (0 left, 10 right) and 7.1/10 on GAL-TAN (0 libertarian/postmaterialist, 10 traditional/authoritarian). GAL-TAN is a cultural axis, so it only approximates the vertical.
days.source: Chapel Hill Expert Survey 2024 (Rovny et al.)

days.title: Privatising healthcare
days.desc: Moving health services from the state to private providers.
days.note: Markets over state provision is firmly right. Little direct effect on personal liberty.

days.title: Mass surveillance
days.desc: Governments monitor communications in bulk to prevent crime.
days.note: Close to the top of the authoritarian axis. Economics barely matters, though it is often backed by the right.

days.title: Open borders
days.desc: Anyone may live and work in any country.
days.note: Left and right libertarians converge on free movement, for different reasons.

days.title: Nationalising railways
days.desc: Bringing rail operations into public ownership.
days.note: Public ownership of infrastructure is a core left position. State control pulls it up the grid.

days.title: Death penalty
days.desc: State execution as punishment for the gravest crimes.
days.note: The state taking life is the sharpest authoritarian act. It is more often backed by the right.

days.title: Abolishing income tax
days.desc: No tax on earnings, with the state funded another way.
days.note: Deep economic right, and strongly libertarian in spirit.

days.title: Public broadcaster
days.desc: A publicly funded national TV and radio service.
days.note: State-funded and left of centre. Public control of media adds a modest authoritarian pull.

days.title: Hate speech laws
days.desc: Criminal penalties for speech targeting protected groups.
days.note: Restricting speech is authoritarian, and the left more often proposes it.

days.title: Flat tax
days.desc: One tax rate for everyone regardless of income.
days.note: Cuts progressive redistribution so right, but says little about personal freedom.

days.title: Free trade deals
days.desc: Agreements removing tariffs between countries.
days.note: Market openness is right, and it reduces state control of trade.

days.title: Banning abortion
days.desc: Making terminating a pregnancy illegal.
days.note: State control over the body is strongly authoritarian. Mostly backed from the right.

days.title: Cashless society
days.desc: Phasing out physical cash in favour of digital payments.
days.note: Little economic content. Traceable payments hand the state more oversight.

days.title: Sugar tax
days.desc: An extra levy on sugary drinks.
days.note: Nudging behaviour through the state is mildly authoritarian. Small economic effect.

days.title: Deregulating planning
days.desc: Making it far easier to build housing without permission.
days.note: Fewer state controls on property owners. Right and libertarian.

days.title: Ending jury trials
days.desc: Replacing juries with judges for most cases.
days.note: Reduces citizen participation in justice. No real economic content.
